That's normal React behavior, not a bug. When a parent re-renders, every child re-renders too by default — React doesn't check if the props actually changed.

Two fixes work together:

1. Wrap the child in `React.memo()`. This tells React to skip the re-render if props look the same.
2. Watch out for new objects or functions. If you write `onClick={() => doThing()}` or `style={{color: 'red'}}` inline, you make a brand new one every render. Even with `React.memo`, that counts as a "different" prop, so the child re-renders anyway.

For functions, wrap them in `useCallback`. For objects, wrap them in `useMemo`. Then `React.memo` on the child can actually catch that nothing changed.
